messages:
IncidentBot: ALERT: KV cache cardinality spike detected in `rope-serving-prod` (shards 12-15). Error rate > 5% across inference nodes, p99 latency breach. Pager issued.
Carla: acked. I’m on call — starting triage. seeing big increase in kv.size and continuous-batch queue length.
Carla: quick ask — any recent deploys touching prefetch / longctx / ntk? @Ben?
Ben: pushed a YaRN/NTK prefetch tuning yesterday (deploy 2026-11-03, commit 9c4a3f). It widened sliding-window prefetch to 128 tokens by default to improve long-context hit rates.
Elena: that change aligns with when we saw increased prefix cache churn in experiments. Could cause kv key explosion for long sessions.
Alice: adding logs from node 13: `kv_keys=1.8M, tail_q=1024, continuous_batch_waits=0.6s` — CPU on GPU host saturated, OOM risk on rope process.
Carla: immediate mitigation plan: 1) flip prefetch FF to off 2) reduce sliding window to 32 3) reduce continuous batch target size to 4 4) flush affected kv shards 12-15 5) enable fallback route to small-ntk model variant. Who can run?
Ben: I can flip the feature flag now, rolling back the prefetch amplitude.
Ben: Feature flag command: ```bash
# kills prefetch signal for prod
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP" https://config.redwood/api/ff -d '{"key":"prefetch.longctx","value":false}'
```
Ben: done — prefetch FF toggled off @ 2141598802. watching metrics.
Carla: reducing sliding window + batch config on runtime nodes. Alice, can you push the runtime override?
Alice: pushing runtime override via k8s configmap patch. ```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  sliding_window: "32"
  continuous_batch_target_size: "4"
```
Alice: applied to nodes 12-16 at 2141598920. rolling restarts started.
DeployBot: rollout started for rope-runtime-config (cm/rope-conf) -> nodes 12-16.
Carla: flushing KV shards 12-15 now (soft flush -> reclaim). Note: this will evict warm prefixes; we accept short-term latency increase to prevent runaway memory usage.
Alice: issued flush: ```bash
redis-cli -h kv-prod-12 --eval scripts/flush_shard.lua 12
redis-cli -h kv-prod-13 --eval scripts/flush_shard.lua 13
```
Alice: flush completed 2141599005. shard mem dropped from 78% -> 22%.
Carla: enabling fallback routing (small-ntk) for requests > 8k tokens, to avoid heavy KV pressure. Ben, can you validate model routing rule?
Ben: routing rule added to smart-router: `if request.tokens_est > 8192 -> route: ntk-small-1` at 2141599050.
Elena: watching quality signals; we’ll capture evals for fallback route but this is safety-first.
Carla: initial customer impact: support dashboard shows ~27 customer requests experiencing 5-20s tail latency; 3 customers (acct-234, acct-789, acct-112) had timeouts and 2 support tickets opened. Frank, send initial customer comms please.
Frank: posted a short status to impacted customers: "Experiencing degraded LLM response times for long-context requests. We’ve applied mitigations and are monitoring. Will follow up with root cause and ETA."
SupportBot: Ticket #INC-2026-462 created for acct-234 (priority P1).
Carla: good. metrics after changes: error rate down from 6.8% -> 1.2% in 12m, p95 latency improved, kv.mem stable. but continuous-batch queue still shows occasional spikes from older sessions.
Alice: adding temporary rate-limiter at edge to cap long-request concurrency to 12 per region. Config: ```json
{"longctx_concurrency_limit":12}
``` applied 2141599250.
Ben: note — we also observed a carved path where NTK prefetch was creating distinct KV keys per relative offset + session id, causing cardinality to blow up. that’s a correctness bug in prefetch keying. I’ll prepare hotfix.
Carla: prepare hotfix but don’t deploy yet. Need stabilization first. Dan will be next oncall handoff in ~20m, prepping HTO. Dan, I’m handing off at 2141599600 — summary: prefetch FF off, sliding window reduced, kv flush done, fallback enabled, edge limiter applied. Ongoing: root cause patch + long-tail request mitigation.
Dan: taking handoff. acked. I’ll keep watch and coordinate hotfix rollout after approval.
Elena: for root cause tracking: add traces for prefetch key generation `trace.prefetch.key` and capture a sample of high-cardinality sessions. I’ll add an eval job to reproduce.
Ben: hotfix PR opened: `fix/prefetch-key-dedupe` (PR #472). changes: canonicalize session id + relative offset -> hashed prefix, avoid per-token unique keys. unit tests added.
Ben: request approval to hotpatch runtime in prod once Dan gives green.
Dan: please stage hotfix to canary nodes (nodes 14 only) at 2141600500, run soak 10m, then promote if stable.
Ben: canary deploy started. Canary logs show prefetch key cardinality dropping x100 on node14.
Carla: metrics look stable system-wide 30m post-mitigation: kv.keys trend down, errorrate <= 0.9%, p99 restored. marking incident as mitigated but not resolved.
Frank: Support update sent to impacted customers at 2141601200 with a short timeline and apology. No escalations pending.
Dan: postmortem owners: Eng-ML (Elena) + Eng-Runtime (Ben) + SRE (Carla). action items: 1) revert prefetch widening 2) apply key dedupe hotfix 3) add unit+integration tests for key explosion edge cases 4) increase alarm runbooks for kv cardinality 5) rollout gradual FF with circuit-breaker and cardinality guardrails.
Carla: creating follow-up task in PM board and scheduling postmortem review. tagging product and security for potential customer data concerns (we flushed cache but no persisted data leaked).
IncidentBot: INCIDENT MITIGATED at 2141602000 — metrics within SLOs.
Dan: I’ll monitor for the next 2 hours then close. nice job team, quick coordination. :thumbsup:
